description: The pie chart displays the category distribution of a dataset, consisting of six distinct slices. The segments are ordered by descending size in a counter-clockwise direction starting from the top vertical axis. The largest slice is colored light red and labeled "chat (41.2%)", followed by a light blue slice labeled "math (21.9%)". Continuing counter-clockwise, the subsequent slices are light green labeled "tooluse (11.6%)", light orange labeled "multi turn chat (9.3%)", light purple labeled "code (9.0%)", and the smallest slice, which is light pink, labeled "instruction follow (6.9%)". The category names and their corresponding percentages are positioned outside the boundaries of their respective slices, with no text placed inside the segments. A legend titled "Categories" is located in the top-left corner, displaying color swatches alongside the category names and their absolute numerical counts: chat (546,526), math (290,496), tooluse (154,358), multi turn chat (123,615), code (119,563), and instruction follow (91,460). None of the slices are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset from the main body of the chart.
